The Committee meets on a regular basis to:", "bbox": [ 184, 147, 882, 198 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Review and endorse changes to the government IT security related regulations, policies and guidelines;", "bbox": [ 186, 221, 868, 254 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Define specific roles and responsibilities relating to IT security; and", "bbox": [ 186, 255, 781, 272 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Provide guidance and assistance to B/Ds in the enforcement of IT security related regulations, policies, and guidelines through the IT Security Working Group (ITSWG).", "bbox": [ 186, 273, 852, 323 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The core members of ISMC comprise representatives from:", "bbox": [ 186, 341, 675, 359 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Digital Policy Office (DPO)", "bbox": [ 186, 382, 458, 399 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Security Bureau (SB)", "bbox": [ 188, 401, 405, 417 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Representative(s) from other B/Ds will be co-opted into the committee on a need basis in relation to specific subject matters. DPO will assist in reviewing and clarifying the documents submitted by B/Ds as required in this document.", "bbox": [ 184, 436, 848, 488 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.1.2 IT Security Working Group (ITSWG)", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 510, 554, 530 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The IT Security Working Group (ITSWG) serves as the executive arm of the ISMC in the promulgation and compliance monitoring of government IT security related regulations, policies and guidelines. The ITSWG was established in May 2000 and its responsibilities are to:", "bbox": [ 184, 551, 882, 619 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Co-ordinate activities aimed at providing guidance and assistance to B/Ds in the enforcement of IT security related regulations, policies and guidelines;", "bbox": [ 186, 638, 878, 671 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Monitor the compliance with the Baseline IT Security Policy at B/Ds;", "bbox": [ 186, 673, 794, 689 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Define and review the IT security related regulations, policies and guidelines; and", "bbox": [ 186, 690, 857, 721 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Promote IT security awareness within the Government.", "bbox": [ 186, 724, 677, 740 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The core members of ITSWG comprise representatives from:", "bbox": [ 186, 760, 690, 777 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Digital Policy Office (DPO)", "bbox": [ 186, 797, 458, 814 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Security Bureau (SB)", "bbox": [ 188, 815, 405, 831 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF)", "bbox": [ 188, 833, 502, 848 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Chief Secretary for Administration’s Office (CSO)", "bbox": [ 186, 850, 642, 866 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "12", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 22 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Representative(s) from other B/Ds will be co-opted into the working group on a need basis in relation to specific subject matters.", "bbox": [ 184, 104, 882, 139 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.1.3 Government Information Security Incident Response Office (GIRO)", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 161, 840, 181 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "To handle information security incidents occurring in B/Ds, an Information Security Incident Response Team (ISIRT) shall be established in each B/D. The Government Information Security Incident Response Office (GIRO) provides central coordination and support to the operation of individual ISIRTs of B/Ds. The GIRO Standing Office serves as the executive arm of GIRO.", "bbox": [ 184, 199, 878, 284 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The GIRO has the following major functions:", "bbox": [ 186, 302, 563, 319 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Maintain a central inventory and oversee the handling of all information security incidents in the Government;", "bbox": [ 186, 336, 882, 369 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Prepare periodic statistics reports on government information security incidents;", "bbox": [ 186, 370, 878, 387 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Act as a central office to co-ordinate the handling of multiple-point security attacks (i.e. simultaneous attacks on different government information systems); and", "bbox": [ 186, 388, 878, 436 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Enable experience sharing and information exchange related to information security incident handling among ISIRTs of different B/Ds.", "bbox": [ 186, 437, 842, 472 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The core members of GIRO comprise representatives from:", "bbox": [ 186, 487, 675, 505 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Digital Policy Office (DPO)", "bbox": [ 186, 520, 458, 537 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Security Bureau (SB)", "bbox": [ 188, 538, 405, 554 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF)", "bbox": [ 186, 556, 502, 574 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.1.4 Government Computer Emergency Response Team Hong Kong (GovCERT.HK)", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 592, 794, 631 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The Government Computer Emergency Response Team Hong Kong (GovCERT.HK) was established in April 2015. In addition to collaborating with GIRO Standing Office in co-ordinating information and cyber security incidents within the Government, it also collaborates with the computer emergency response team community in sharing incident information and threat intelligence, and exchanging best practices to strengthen information and cyber security capabilities in the region. GovCERT.HK has the following major functions:", "bbox": [ 184, 650, 865, 768 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Disseminate security alerts on impending and actual threats to B/Ds; and", "bbox": [ 186, 785, 820, 802 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Act as a bridge between the Hong Kong Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) and other computer security incident response teams (CSIRT) in handling cyber security incidents.", "bbox": [ 186, 803, 872, 854 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "13", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 23 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.1.5 Bureaux/Departments", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 105, 401, 124 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall be responsible for the security protection of their information assets and information systems. The roles and responsibilities of IT security staff within a B/D are detailed in Section 5.2 - Departmental IT Security Organisation.", "bbox": [ 184, 147, 877, 198 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2 Departmental IT Security Organisation", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 219, 563, 240 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "This section explains the individual roles and responsibilities of a departmental IT security organisation. In order to have sufficient segregation of duties, multiple roles should not be assigned to an individual unless there is a resource limitation.", "bbox": [ 184, 261, 858, 313 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The following diagram describes a sample departmental IT security management framework:", "bbox": [ 186, 335, 850, 367 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "image", "img_path": "images/8e5636b399f4c5cb9c63c626fb74ab826357f810d0a12087dd659eb43f710a9c.jpg", "image_caption": [ "An Example Organisation Chart for Departmental IT Security Management1" ], "image_footnote": [], "bbox": [ 198, 370, 830, 639 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2.1 Departmental IT Security Officer (DITSO)", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 709, 600, 730 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Head of B/D shall appoint an officer at D3 level or above from the senior management to be the Departmental IT Security Officer (DITSO) and responsible for IT security. As the senior management of the B/D, the DITSO shall participate in the overall steering of IT security matters of the B/D. The DITSO shall also understand the B/D’s priorities, the importance of the B/D’s information systems and data assets, and the level of security that shall be achieved.", "bbox": [ 184, 749, 865, 833 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 48, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "14", "bbox": [ 862, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "page_footnote", "text": "1 The actual IT Security Management structure may vary according to the circumstances of each organisation.", "bbox": [ 115, 898, 867, 915 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 24 }, { "type": "text", "text": "", "bbox": [ 186, 104, 702, 122 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If a B/D does not have a directorate officer at D3 level or above, the highest rank directorate officer of the B/D shall assume the position of DITSO so as to uphold the principle of ensuring accountability in IT security.", "bbox": [ 184, 137, 880, 190 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "To better equip the designated DITSOs with security management and related technology knowledge or skills, SB and DPO will provide training to DITSOs to facilitate them in carrying out their duties and DITSOs shall attend the designated training. The roles and responsibilities of DITSO shall be clearly defined, which include but are not limited to the following:", "bbox": [ 184, 203, 855, 287 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Establish and maintain an information protection program to assist all staff in the protection of the information and information systems they use;", "bbox": [ 186, 310, 880, 344 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Establish a proper security governance process to evaluate, direct, monitor and communicate the IT security related activities within the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 348, 862, 381 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Drive regular discussions on IT security issues at the senior management level to acquire adequate support and resources;", "bbox": [ 186, 385, 878, 419 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Lead in the establishment, maintenance and implementation of IT security policies, standards, procedures and guidelines;", "bbox": [ 186, 422, 825, 456 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Oversee, monitor, review and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of IT security management throughout every stage of IT operations;", "bbox": [ 186, 460, 843, 494 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Monitor and ensure compliance with the government IT security requirements, including overseeing the satisfactory completion of security audit exercises of the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 497, 860, 546 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Oversee the overall IT security awareness and training programmes within the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 551, 857, 583 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Co-ordinate with other B/Ds on IT security issues;", "bbox": [ 186, 588, 631, 605 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Oversee the overall IT risk management process within the B/D, including overseeing the satisfactory completion of information security risk assessments and privacy impact assessments as well as subsequent rectifications and responding to the evolving risk landscape, regulatory changes, technological advancements, and the system criticality;", "bbox": [ 186, 609, 863, 692 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Oversee the IT security threat detection and monitoring process and the threat intelligence activities of the B/D, including dissemination of security alerts on impending and actual threats from the GIRO to responsible parties within the B/D and relevant project teams; and", "bbox": [ 186, 695, 855, 762 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Initiate investigation and rectification in case of breach of security and coordinate the required submission of incident reports to the Director of Bureau.", "bbox": [ 186, 765, 855, 800 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2.2 Information Security Steering Committee", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 819, 586, 838 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The senior management of B/Ds shall have an appreciation of IT security, its problems and resolutions. Senior management should consider setting up of an information security steering committee which reports to DITSO, or including", "bbox": [ 186, 862, 836, 913 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "15", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 25 }, { "type": "text", "text": "information security as one of the regular discussion items in management meetings. The responsibilities of the committee include:", "bbox": [ 184, 104, 878, 139 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Demonstrate leadership in promoting and prioritising IT security within the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 162, 878, 179 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Direct and enforce the development of security measures;", "bbox": [ 186, 184, 692, 200 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Provide the necessary resources required for the measures to be implemented;", "bbox": [ 186, 204, 855, 221 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Foster the proper, orderly and secure functioning of all information systems of the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 225, 862, 258 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Ensure participation and accountability at all levels of management, administrative, technical and operational staff, and provide full support to them;", "bbox": [ 186, 262, 872, 297 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Foster a culture of security awareness and accountability throughout the B/D; and", "bbox": [ 186, 300, 850, 332 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Ensure B/D’s IT security strategies align with the business objectives.", "bbox": [ 186, 337, 789, 355 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "If B/Ds choose not to set up an information security steering committee, DITSO should undertake the responsibilities of the committee.", "bbox": [ 186, 376, 842, 412 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2.3 Departmental Security Officer (DSO)", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 434, 549, 455 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The Head of B/D will designate a Departmental Security Officer (DSO) to perform the departmental security related duties. The DSO will take the role of an executive to:", "bbox": [ 186, 476, 873, 525 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Discharge responsibilities for all aspects of security for the B/D; and", "bbox": [ 186, 550, 779, 568 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Advise on the set up and review of the security policy.", "bbox": [ 186, 571, 665, 589 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The DSO may take on the role of the DITSO. Alternatively, in those B/Ds where someone else is appointed, the DITSO shall collaborate with the DSO to oversee the IT security of the B/D.", "bbox": [ 184, 611, 877, 662 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2.4 Departmental Information Security Incident Response Team (ISIRT) Commander", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 683, 845, 722 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The ISIRT is the central focal point for co-ordinating the handling of information security incidents occurring within the respective B/D. The Head of B/D should designate an officer from the senior management to be the ISIRT Commander. The ISIRT Commander should have the authority to appoint core team members for the ISIRT. The responsibilities of an ISIRT Commander include:", "bbox": [ 184, 745, 872, 829 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Provide overall supervision and co-ordination of information security incident handling for all information systems within the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 852, 857, 887 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "16", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 26 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Make decisions on critical matters such as damage containment, system recovery, the engagement of external parties and the extent of involvement, and service resumption logistics after recovery;", "bbox": [ 186, 107, 868, 156 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Trigger the departmental disaster recovery procedure where appropriate, depending on the impact of the incident on the business operation of the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 160, 852, 193 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Provide management endorsement on the provision of resources for the incident handling process;", "bbox": [ 186, 197, 872, 230 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Provide management endorsement in respect of the line-to-take for publicity on the incident;", "bbox": [ 186, 235, 867, 268 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Collaborate with GIRO in reporting information security incidents for central recording and necessary follow-up actions; and", "bbox": [ 186, 272, 850, 306 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Facilitate experience and information sharing within the B/D on information security incident handling and related matters.", "bbox": [ 186, 310, 842, 343 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.2.5 IT Security Management Unit", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 366, 468, 386 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall establish an IT security management unit which reports to DITSO and assists DITSO in discharging his/her duties. The size and composition of the unit may vary among B/Ds depending on the business and operational needs of B/Ds. The responsibilities of the IT security management unit include:", "bbox": [ 184, 405, 853, 473 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assist DITSO in overseeing the security governance process for the IT security related activities within the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 494, 865, 529 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Assist DITSO in the IT security management process for all IT operations of the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 532, 873, 564 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Assist DITSO in developing, establishing, and maintaining the overall IT security strategy and roadmap for the B/D, including formulating IT security policies, baselines, standards, directives, etc.;", "bbox": [ 186, 569, 845, 620 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Co-ordinate security awareness and training programmes within the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 624, 816, 640 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Co-ordinate the implementation of IT security initiatives and monitor the status of IT security processes to ensure the effectiveness of IT security management and compliance with government security requirements;", "bbox": [ 188, 644, 865, 695 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Facilitate IT security threat and risk management activities and support disaster recovery and business continuity planning functions relating to IT security;", "bbox": [ 186, 699, 867, 732 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Co-ordinate security incident investigation and rectification;", "bbox": [ 186, 736, 712, 752 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Liaise with other B/Ds and parties on IT security matters; and", "bbox": [ 186, 757, 726, 774 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Perform any other duties as directed by the DITSO.", "bbox": [ 186, 777, 640, 795 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 878, 78 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "17", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 880, 940 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 27 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3 Other Roles", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 104, 309, 123 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.1 IT Security Administrators", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 147, 448, 167 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "IT Security Administrators shall be responsible for providing security and risk management related support services. His / her responsibilities also include:", "bbox": [ 184, 190, 826, 225 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assist in identifying and mitigating system vulnerabilities;", "bbox": [ 186, 247, 699, 265 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Assist in the patch management process;", "bbox": [ 186, 269, 554, 286 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Conduct security administrative tasks, such as implementing access controls and managing user privileges;", "bbox": [ 186, 288, 875, 323 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Maintain and review audit logs;", "bbox": [ 186, 326, 482, 344 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Monitor threat intelligence sources and stay updated on emerging security threats; and", "bbox": [ 186, 348, 823, 380 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Operate and maintain security tools and systems, such as intrusion detection and prevention systems.", "bbox": [ 186, 385, 873, 419 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The IT Security Administrator should not be the same person as the System Administrator. There should be a segregation of duties between the IT Security Administrator and the System Administrator.", "bbox": [ 186, 441, 840, 493 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Although the IT Security Administrators are responsible for managing the audit logs, they should not tamper with or change any audit log.", "bbox": [ 186, 514, 882, 549 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds may appoint an IT Security Auditor, who will be responsible for auditing the work of the IT Security Administrators to ensure that they perform their duties due diligently.", "bbox": [ 184, 570, 865, 621 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.2 Information Owners", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 644, 388, 663 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Information Owners shall be the collators and the owners of information stored in information systems. Their primary responsibility is to:", "bbox": [ 184, 686, 855, 721 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Determine the data classifications, the authorised data usage, and the corresponding security requirements for protection of the information.", "bbox": [ 186, 744, 791, 778 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "18", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 28 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.3 LAN/System Administrators", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 104, 467, 124 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "LAN/System Administrators shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration, operation and configuration of the computer systems and network in B/Ds, whereas Internet System Administrators are responsible for the related tasks for their Internetfacing information systems. Their responsibilities include:", "bbox": [ 184, 147, 882, 215 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Implement the security mechanisms and controls in accordance with procedures/guidelines established by the DITSO.", "bbox": [ 186, 237, 778, 272 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.4 Application Development & Maintenance Team", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 294, 650, 313 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The Application Development & Maintenance Team shall be responsible for producing quality systems with the use of quality procedures, techniques and tools. Their responsibilities include:", "bbox": [ 184, 336, 865, 387 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Liaise with the Information Owner in order to define and implement system security requirements during the development and maintenance of applications; and", "bbox": [ 186, 410, 867, 460 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Ensure quality procedures, techniques, and tools are used to produce secure systems.", "bbox": [ 188, 464, 835, 498 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "5.3.5 Users", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 520, 248, 539 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Users of information systems shall be the staff authorised to access and use the information. Users shall be accountable for all their activities. Responsibilities of a user include:", "bbox": [ 186, 563, 873, 613 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Attend security awareness and training programmes directed by the B/D;", "bbox": [ 186, 637, 815, 655 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Know, understand, follow and apply all the possible and available security mechanisms to the maximum extent possible;", "bbox": [ 186, 658, 826, 692 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Prevent leakage and unauthorised access to information under his/her custody; and", "bbox": [ 186, 696, 858, 728 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Safekeep computing and storage devices, and protect them from unauthorised access or malicious attack with his/her best effort.", "bbox": [ 186, 733, 853, 766 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "19", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 882, 940 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "header", "text": "GOVERNMENT ORGANISATION STRUCTURE ON INFORMATION SECURITY", "bbox": [ 519, 49, 880, 78 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 29 }, { "type": "text", "text": "6. CORE SECURITY PRINCIPLES", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 105, 539, 124 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "This section introduces some generally accepted principles that address information security from a very high-level viewpoint. These principles are fundamental in nature and rarely change. B/Ds shall observe these principles for developing, implementing and understanding security policies. The principles listed below are by no means exhaustive.", "bbox": [ 184, 147, 870, 231 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Information System Security Objectives", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 254, 576, 271 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Information system security objectives or goals are described in terms of three overall objectives: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability. Security policies and measures shall be developed and implemented according to these objectives.", "bbox": [ 216, 273, 872, 340 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "These security objectives guide the standards, procedures and controls used in all aspects of security design and security solutions. In short, for an information system, only authorised users shall be allowed to know, gain access, make changes to, or delete the information stored or processed by the information system. The system shall also be accessible and usable upon demand by the authorised users.", "bbox": [ 220, 355, 878, 455 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Risk-Based Approach", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 474, 420, 492 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A risk-based approach shall be adopted to identify, prioritise and address the security risks of information systems in a consistent and effective manner. Proper security measures shall be implemented according to the classified protection of IT security described in Section 7.2 (b) to protect information assets and systems and mitigate security risks to an acceptable level.", "bbox": [ 220, 494, 848, 579 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The risk-based approach usually involves a risk assessment process and a risk treatment process which can be embedded within different processes, such as project management, vulnerability management, incident management, problem management, or even on an impromptu basis for a given identified specific topic. The risk assessment process involves:", "bbox": [ 221, 596, 877, 680 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(a) establishing and maintaining the risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing the information security risk assessment;", "bbox": [ 226, 682, 855, 714 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(b) identifying the risk owners and the risks associated with the loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability of information;", "bbox": [ 226, 714, 820, 747 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(c) analysing the risks by determining the risk levels based on the potential impact and likelihood of occurrence;", "bbox": [ 226, 747, 852, 780 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(d) evaluating the risks by comparing the results of risk analysis with the established criteria and prioritising the analysed risks for treatment.", "bbox": [ 226, 781, 835, 814 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The risk treatment process shall be applied to select appropriate risk treatment options and determine the necessary controls to implement the chosen options. The risk-based process shall ensure all necessary controls are included,", "bbox": [ 221, 833, 865, 884 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "header", "text": "CORE SECURITY PRINCIPLES", "bbox": [ 630, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "20", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 30 }, { "type": "text", "text": "formulate a risk treatment plan and obtain the risk owner’s approval of the plan and acceptance of the residual information security risks.", "bbox": [ 221, 91, 872, 126 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "A risk owner is responsible for the assessment, management, and monitoring of an identified risk as well as implementation of selected controls to the risk.", "bbox": [ 221, 147, 875, 181 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Security-by-Design Approach", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 204, 487, 221 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The security-by-design approach shall be adopted to incorporate security requirements into the SDLC, ensuring that information systems and applications are implemented with appropriate security and data protection measures. Security shall be considered and introduced throughout all phases of the development process in order to minimise rework efforts.", "bbox": [ 220, 224, 880, 307 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The security-by-design approach is a software and hardware development approach that seeks to minimise system vulnerabilities and reduce the attack surface through designing and building security in every phase of the SDLC. This includes incorporating security specifications in the design, continuous security evaluation at each phase and adherence to best practices. Specific to IT security, security by design addresses the IT protection considerations throughout a system’s lifecycle. This includes security design specifically to strengthen the IT resiliency of the system. Therefore, B/Ds shall adopt the security-by-design approach as far as possible.", "bbox": [ 220, 325, 878, 476 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Prevention, Detection, Response and Recovery", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 498, 631, 514 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Information security is a combination of preventive, detective, response and recovery measures. Preventive measures avoid or deter the occurrence of an undesirable event. Detective measures identify the occurrence of an undesirable event. Response measures refer to co-ordinated actions to contain damage when an undesirable event (or incident) occurs. Recovery measures restore the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information systems to their expected state.", "bbox": [ 215, 517, 882, 633 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Prevention is the first line of defence. Deployment of proper security protection and measures helps to reduce the risks of security incidents. However, when the prevention safeguards are defeated, B/Ds shall be able to detect security incidents rapidly and respond quickly to contain the damage. The information systems and data shall be recovered in a timely manner. Therefore, B/Ds shall designate appropriate personnel to manage IT security as well as plan for the information security incident handling.", "bbox": [ 221, 655, 880, 772 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Protection of Information while being Processed, in Transit, and in Storage Security measures shall be considered and implemented as appropriate to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information while it is being processed, in transit, and in storage2. As an example, wireless communication without protection is vulnerable to attacks, and security measures shall be adopted when transmitting classified information.", "bbox": [ 186, 794, 877, 848 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "header", "text": "CORE SECURITY PRINCIPLES", "bbox": [ 630, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "21", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 31 }, { "type": "text", "text": "", "bbox": [ 220, 91, 810, 142 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": "When B/Ds formulate security measures, they shall carefully consider and assess the risk of unauthorised modification, destruction or disclosure of information and denial of access to information in different states.", "bbox": [ 221, 162, 831, 215 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Assumption of Insecurity about External Systems", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 236, 658, 254 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In general, an external system shall be assumed to be insecure. When B/Ds’ information assets or information systems connect with external systems, B/Ds shall implement security measures, using either physical or logical means, according to the business requirements and the associated risk levels.", "bbox": [ 216, 256, 870, 325 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The external systems may not be designed, developed and maintained according to government security requirements. Therefore, B/Ds shall consider implementing multi-level defence when information assets or information systems connect with external systems. Consider any data you receive from an external system, including input from users, that may be a potential source of attack. Information systems shall be partitioned or segregated accordingly, and different access controls and levels of protection should be applied commensurate to the required security level of the systems.", "bbox": [ 220, 346, 878, 479 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Resilience for Crucial Information Systems", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 500, 605, 518 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": "All crucial information systems shall be resilient to stand against major disruptive events, with measures in place to detect disruption, minimise damage and rapidly respond and recover. Damage containment shall be considered in the resilience plan and implemented as appropriate with an aim to limit the scope, magnitude and impact of an incident for effective recovery.", "bbox": [ 220, 520, 877, 606 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Damage containment means the implementation of security controls to limit the impact of damage arising from a security incident. The resilience of an information system refers to its ability to continue to operate under adverse conditions or stress, even if in a degraded or debilitated state while maintaining essential operational capabilities. It also includes the recovery of the system to an effective operational posture in a time frame consistent with business needs.", "bbox": [ 220, 626, 875, 727 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "22", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 940 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 342, 64 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "header", "text": "CORE SECURITY PRINCIPLES", "bbox": [ 630, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "page_footnote", "text": "For the purpose of this document, \"information in storage\" refers to those data stored in non-volatile media that retains the information when power is shut off. Non-volatile media includes, but is not limited to, hard disk, solid state drive, optical disk, magnetic tape, USB flash drive and Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (NVRAM). The data residing in non-volatile media of any IT equipment like servers, workstations, notebooks, mobile devices, printers, network devices are regarded as information in storage. For those data that stored in volatile media (e.g. RAM) which gradually loses its information when power is shut off, they are not regarded as information in storage.", "bbox": [ 114, 816, 873, 916 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 215, 941 ], "page_idx": 32 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Auditability and Accountability", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 92, 504, 109 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Security shall require auditability and accountability. Auditability refers to the ability to verify the activities in an information system. Evidence used for verification can take the form of audit trails, system logs, alarms, or other notifications. Accountability refers to the ability to audit the actions of all parties and processes which interact with information systems. Roles and responsibilities shall be clearly defined, identified, and authorised at a level commensurate with the sensitivity of information.", "bbox": [ 220, 112, 867, 230 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Auditability helps to reconstruct the complete behavioural history of a system and, hence, is useful for discovering and investigating a system during a security incident. Accountability is often accomplished by uniquely identifying a single individual so as to enable tracing his/her activities on an information system.", "bbox": [ 221, 252, 882, 318 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Continual Improvement", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 189, 338, 440, 355 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "text", "text": "To be responsive and adaptive to changing environments and technologies, a continual improvement process shall be implemented for monitoring, reviewing and improving the effectiveness and efficiency of IT security management. Performance of security measures shall be evaluated periodically to determine whether the IT security objectives are met.", "bbox": [ 221, 359, 875, 442 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall identify the information security processes and controls to be monitored and measured and determine the methods for monitoring, measuring and evaluating the results. Regular reviews shall be performed on the security measures to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness. The output of security reviews shall include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the security measures where appropriate.", "bbox": [ 220, 456, 867, 574 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "23", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "header", "text": "CORE SECURITY PRINCIPLES", "bbox": [ 630, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 33 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7. MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 105, 600, 124 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Head of B/D shall put in place effective security arrangements to ensure information systems and assets of the Government are safeguarded, and IT services are delivered securely.", "bbox": [ 186, 147, 882, 199 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.1 General Management", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 221, 400, 241 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(a) Roles and Responsibilities", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 263, 445, 284 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall apply core security principles and best practices concerning the issue of checks and balances in information security management. Information security shall be considered in all stages of the project management, regardless of the project type.", "bbox": [ 184, 306, 880, 359 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Regardless of the sources of funding of information systems, B/Ds shall ensure all of their information systems, including infrastructure facilities and departmental shared IT services, are properly protected in accordance with their risk levels. The classified protection of IT security mentioned in Section 7.2 (b) shall be adopted to enable effective IT security risk management for information systems. In addition, B/Ds shall ensure that security protection is responsive and adaptive to changing environments and technology.", "bbox": [ 184, 375, 882, 492 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall define their own departmental IT security management framework with reference to Section 5.2 Departmental IT Security Organisation. A senior and key personnel in the B/D should be assigned the responsibility for ensuring that appropriate policies and procedures are developed and applied and that necessary checks and balances on proper administration and operation of the policies and procedures are in place. B/Ds should make reference to the departmental IT security management framework, policies and procedures when assigning responsibilities.", "bbox": [ 184, 513, 880, 631 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Staff with assigned responsibilities may delegate security tasks to others, but they remain ultimately accountable for ensuring that adequate security measures have been implemented. However, staff with assigned responsibilities should ensure that the delegated tasks are performed by appropriate staff in terms of capability, knowledge, experience and seniority. They should check that any delegated tasks have been performed properly. The details of delegation shall be documented and periodically reviewed.", "bbox": [ 184, 652, 873, 770 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "24", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "header", "text": "MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES", "bbox": [ 586, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 34 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(b) Segregation of Duties", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 91, 400, 111 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Segregation of duties is the practice of dividing the steps in a function among different individuals so as to keep out the possibility of a single individual from subverting a process. There shall be sufficient segregation of duties with roles and responsibilities clearly defined so as to minimise the chance that a single individual will have the authority to execute and control all security functions and/or crucial operations of an information system.", "bbox": [ 184, 134, 868, 235 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In situations where segregation of duties is not practicable due to reasons such as a limited number of staff available or other technical limitations, compensating controls should be put in place to provide the equivalent safeguards, e.g. by maintaining appropriate logging on critical operations conducted by the staff together with random inspection and/or regular review on the log file by an appropriate level of authority.", "bbox": [ 186, 256, 863, 356 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(c) Budgeting", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 378, 294, 399 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall control the budget to ensure sufficient resource allocation to support the implementation of necessary security safeguards for security protection. Management should develop information security budget plans, projections and resource allocations based on short-term and long-term objectives or goals. Resources should be allocated to protect information systems according to their risk levels.", "bbox": [ 186, 419, 872, 520 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(d) Rights for Information Examination", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 546, 534, 567 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall reserve the right to examine all information stored in or transmitted by government information systems, including emails, file directories, and access records to discussion boards, newsgroups and websites, in compliance with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance. This examination helps assure compliance with internal policies, supports internal investigations, and facilitates security management of government information systems.", "bbox": [ 184, 581, 873, 682 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "7.2 Security Risk Management", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 703, 452, 724 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(a) Risk-based Approach", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 743, 398, 763 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall adopt a risk-based approach to information security to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets and all other security aspects of information systems in facing the changing environment and technologies. By applying some simple measures, B/Ds should be able to effectively mitigate and control potential information security risks associated with human and/or operation problems to an acceptable and manageable level. B/Ds shall consider the best practices for possible adoption with regard to their individual business and operation environments.", "bbox": [ 184, 782, 880, 914 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "header", "text": "MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES", "bbox": [ 586, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "25", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 35 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(b) Classified Protection of IT Security", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 91, 531, 111 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "To ensure all government information systems are duly protected by security controls which are commensurate with the risk levels of information systems, B/Ds shall adopt classified protection of IT security by assessing the classifications of all their information systems, including infrastructure facilities and departmental shared IT services, regardless of the source of their funding and implementing tiered security controls according to the system classifications, which include Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 information systems. B/Ds shall adopt all the mandatory security requirements set out in this document for ordinary information systems and additionally adopt the more stringent security requirements set out in Appendix C for Tier 2 and Tier 3 information systems. B/Ds shall ensure that the classifications of information systems align with their business objectives across the entire life cycle of the information systems.", "bbox": [ 184, 130, 880, 329 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Tier 2 information systems refer to the information systems which are crucial to the operations of the Government or society and whose failure or disruption will result in a serious impact on government operations or may cause public turmoil and catastrophes. B/Ds should consider the data classification and the consequences of service disruption when determining the criticality. The criticality should be assessed on various aspects including:", "bbox": [ 186, 343, 872, 442 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Defence/security risks (e.g. harm to human lives or properties, personal privacy, inability to carry out statutory duties and maintain law and order).", "bbox": [ 186, 443, 877, 476 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Financial implications (e.g. the potential to reduce economic growth, financial loss of the Government).", "bbox": [ 186, 481, 863, 513 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Government Image (e.g. effect on government reputation, public confidence).", "bbox": [ 186, 518, 857, 536 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Interdependency (e.g. degradation of services of one system might result in service disruption to another information system).", "bbox": [ 186, 539, 840, 573 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In addition, B/Ds should include other aspects that apply to their information systems in the assessment of system classification. The assessment should be made with respect to the scope (i.e. number of users affected), severity (i.e. the consequences of disruption or destruction), downtime tolerance (i.e. the point that the service disruption could have a serious impact) and the largest potential business impact that would result from the failure or disruption of the information system.", "bbox": [ 184, 592, 877, 693 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Furthermore, there are a number of essential services that are critical to the functioning and security of a society and its economy. Tier 3 information systems refer to the Tier 2 information systems which are directly related to the provision of essential service concerned and whose disruption or destruction may cause serious harm to the economy, people’s livelihood, public safety, etc.", "bbox": [ 186, 707, 873, 791 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall determine the classifications of information systems during the project initiation stage. When assessing the classifications of information systems, B/Ds shall make reference to the considerations in Appendix B. The assessment details of system classification of all information systems shall be properly documented. The information system classifications shall be endorsed by the Heads of B/Ds or their explicitly delegated officer at directorate level.", "bbox": [ 184, 804, 882, 906 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "header", "text": "MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES", "bbox": [ 586, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "26", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 36 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(c) IT Security Risk Management Framework", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 91, 594, 111 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "To ensure security risk assessments of B/Ds are performed and monitored in a structured manner, B/Ds should adopt the following IT security risk management framework, which encompasses a series of risk management processes and utilise risk registers to achieve effective management and communication about IT security risks. A highlight of the framework is given below for reference.", "bbox": [ 184, 130, 878, 215 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Departmental context establishment – establishing the B/D’s IT security risk management context, which includes the B/D’s risk appetite and tolerance.", "bbox": [ 186, 230, 850, 263 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Risk assessment – performing security risk assessments specified in Section 20.2 (a) for all information systems of the B/D, which identify IT security risks of an information system according to risk sources (e.g. vulnerabilities, threats) and events (e.g. incident scenarios), determine the level of identified risks based on their impact and likelihood, prioritise the analysed risks for risk treatment, and document the prioritised risks in the risk registers of information systems.", "bbox": [ 186, 267, 877, 367 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Risk treatment – determining the appropriate risk treatment (e.g. risk reduction, avoidance, transfer, and acceptance) for each risk of information systems to reduce it to a level within the B/D’s risk appetite and documenting the treatment in the risk registers of information systems.", "bbox": [ 186, 370, 878, 436 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Risk correlation, aggregation and normalisation – consolidating individual risk registers of information systems into a departmental IT security risk register by performing risk correlation, aggregation, and normalisation in the departmental context to facilitate the monitoring and communication about IT security risks in a B/D.", "bbox": [ 186, 441, 882, 521 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Risk monitoring and reporting – monitoring the departmental IT security risks and the corresponding risk treatment and reporting them to DITSO and other relevant parties.", "bbox": [ 186, 526, 862, 577 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "For more information about the IT security risk management framework, please refer to the following document for details:", "bbox": [ 186, 596, 840, 630 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Practice Guide for IT Security Risk Management", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 188, 646, 655, 664 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Available at ITG InfoStation", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 223, 667, 465, 683 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(https://itginfo.ccgo.hksarg/content/itsecure/techcorner/practices.shtml)", "bbox": [ 221, 687, 806, 705 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "27", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 940 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "header", "text": "MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES", "bbox": [ 586, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 37 }, { "type": "text", "text": "IT SECURITY POLICIES", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 105, 467, 124 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall define and enforce their IT security policies to provide management direction and support for protecting information systems and assets in accordance with the business needs and security requirements.", "bbox": [ 184, 147, 855, 199 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "8.1 Management Direction for IT Security", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 221, 559, 241 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(a) Departmental IT Security Policy", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 260, 502, 281 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Essentially, IT security policy shall set the minimum standards of a security specification and state what aspects are of paramount importance to the organisation. Thus, IT security policy shall be treated as the basic rules to be observed as mandatory while there can still be other desirable measures to enhance security.", "bbox": [ 184, 303, 880, 370 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall establish the departmental IT security policy based on the Baseline IT Security Policy as the basis for development.", "bbox": [ 186, 391, 848, 426 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The departmental IT security policy shall cover the proper use of the information systems, data assets, network resources, IT services and facilities, as well as the procedures to prevent and respond to security incidents. Drafting of the policy shall consider the following:", "bbox": [ 184, 448, 873, 516 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• B/Ds’ own requirements on security.", "bbox": [ 186, 538, 527, 555 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Prevailing government IT security requirements as specified in Section 2.3.", "bbox": [ 186, 560, 838, 577 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance.", "bbox": [ 186, 581, 517, 596 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Code on Access to Information.", "bbox": [ 186, 601, 487, 618 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Information on Record Management in the Manual of Office Practice.", "bbox": [ 186, 623, 794, 639 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The drafting of the policy shall additionally consider the following:", "bbox": [ 186, 662, 739, 680 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Goals and direction of the Government of HKSAR.", "bbox": [ 186, 683, 645, 700 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Existing policies, rules, regulations and laws of the Government of HKSAR.", "bbox": [ 186, 705, 847, 721 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• B/Ds’ own requirements and needs.", "bbox": [ 188, 726, 519, 741 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Implementation, distribution and enforcement issues.", "bbox": [ 186, 746, 660, 764 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should set up procedures to provide prompt assistance in investigative matters relating to breaches of security and policy implementation issues. Establishing a Departmental Information Security Incident Response Team (ISIRT) and setting up a security incident response plan can improve the effectiveness of the policy.", "bbox": [ 184, 783, 872, 851 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "28", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 342, 64 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY POLICIES", "bbox": [ 682, 49, 882, 64 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 38 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(b) Evaluation and Periodic Review", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 91, 499, 110 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Review of information security policies, standards, guidelines and procedures shall be conducted periodically. Results and proposed changes from reviews shall be evaluated and endorsed by related parties to ensure the necessary requirements are incorporated. B/Ds may consider hiring external qualified IT security auditors or consultants to review or assist in the development of the information security documents to improve the quality and completeness of the documents.", "bbox": [ 184, 134, 863, 235 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The development of information security documents without ongoing support will eventually leave them unattended and even outdated over time. In fact, some issues may diminish in importance while the new ones continually appear. Hence, frequent reviews of the information security documents can help ensure that the policy meets the latest requirements and copes with technological changes.", "bbox": [ 184, 252, 880, 337 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(c) Communication with Users", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 357, 453, 378 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall promulgate their own IT Security Policy. A mechanism for the delivery of the policy shall be established to ensure ease of accessibility and availability to all staff, functional groups and management. B/Ds shall ensure that they are fully aware of the IT security policy so that they can carry out their duties and meet the government security requirements.", "bbox": [ 184, 400, 878, 485 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "No policy shall be considered implemented unless users or related parties have commitment and communication. Hence, B/Ds should make sure that users and related parties:", "bbox": [ 186, 505, 842, 557 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Are informed of the policy by briefing or orientation when they newly join.", "bbox": [ 186, 580, 838, 598 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Are invited to participate in developing the policy proposals.", "bbox": [ 186, 601, 721, 618 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Are trained with the skills needed to follow the policy.", "bbox": [ 186, 623, 670, 638 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Are periodically reminded of and refreshed for security threats or issues.", "bbox": [ 186, 643, 813, 659 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "• Are provided with policy guidance in manageable units.", "bbox": [ 186, 664, 684, 682 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In order to help an end user understand his / her responsibilities in IT security, B/Ds should develop a departmental end user instruction document on IT security, which highlights the security requirements that are related to an end user in a simple instruction format. A sample template is available in Appendix A – Sample IT Security End User Instructions.", "bbox": [ 186, 703, 872, 788 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "29", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 882, 940 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY POLICIES", "bbox": [ 682, 49, 880, 64 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 39 }, { "type": "text", "text": "9. HUMAN RESOURCE SECURITY", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 105, 551, 124 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Positively cultivating a strong security culture is crucial for enhancing B/D’s security posture, reducing risks, complying with regulations, and building a resilient and trusted environment across the Government. B/Ds shall ensure that staff engaged in government work are suitable for the roles, understand their responsibilities and are aware of information security risks. B/Ds shall protect the government interests in the process of new, changing or terminating employment.", "bbox": [ 184, 147, 875, 249 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "9.1 New, During or Termination of Employment", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 267, 620, 287 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(a) IT Security Responsibilities", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 312, 458, 334 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "IT security roles and responsibilities shall be communicated to all staff when they are assigned a new post, and periodically throughout their term of employment. B/Ds shall ensure that all staff:", "bbox": [ 184, 348, 855, 398 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "are informed of the departmental IT security policy by briefing or orientation when they newly join; and", "bbox": [ 188, 414, 853, 449 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "are aware of and periodically reminded of their IT security responsibilities and the government security requirements.", "bbox": [ 188, 454, 865, 488 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(b) Information Dissemination", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 506, 450, 526 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "An effective information dissemination mechanism shall be in place to ensure all personnel involved are fully aware of the respective policies and procedures governing their authority and usage of information systems.", "bbox": [ 186, 549, 848, 601 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(c) Training", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 618, 277, 639 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Proper security training and updates on IT security policy shall be provided to all staff regularly, including users, developers, system administrators, and security administrators who are engaged in government work to strengthen their awareness of information security. The awareness training may be in any form, such as classroom training, computer based training or self-paced learning. Users should be made aware of the training resources available on the Cyber Learning Centre Plus (CLC Plus) of the Civil Service College, which also includes general IT security related courseware and a self-assessment package for participants.", "bbox": [ 184, 659, 885, 795 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds may make reference to the resources when providing tailor-made training and materials to their staff or contractors in accordance with their own business and operation requirements. More information about CLC Plus is available at https://www.clcplus.csc.gov.hk.", "bbox": [ 184, 812, 870, 879 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 48, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "header", "text": "HUMAN RESOURCE SECURITY", "bbox": [ 621, 49, 880, 64 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "30", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 882, 941 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 40 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Staff may also raise their security awareness by participating in security drills, attending seminars, showcases or visiting theme pages containing security intelligence information and general security information (e.g. Cyber Security Information Portal, InfoSec website). B/Ds shall participate in the IT security awareness activities designated by DPO.", "bbox": [ 184, 91, 828, 174 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Proper education and training should also be provided to the system administrators in implementing the IT security procedures. System administrators should know how to protect their systems from attack and unauthorised use. System administrators shall have a defined procedure for reporting security problems.", "bbox": [ 184, 196, 863, 265 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should consider formulating an IT security training programme to enable the provision of targeted and structured IT security awareness activities to their staff.", "bbox": [ 186, 285, 862, 321 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "An IT security training programme should include but is not limited to the following:", "bbox": [ 186, 342, 794, 376 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(i) Programme objectives", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 398, 416, 416 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should establish objectives for the IT security awareness programme. The objectives should be aligned with the overall IT security strategy of the B/D.", "bbox": [ 184, 418, 842, 453 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(ii) Target Audience", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 472, 371, 488 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should identify the specific groups or roles required to participate in the training activities. B/Ds should consider different levels of technical expertise, job functions, and needs to tailor the training content accordingly.", "bbox": [ 186, 492, 865, 543 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(iii) Training Approach", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 560, 389, 579 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "The design of training materials and content should be aligned with the objectives and target audience. Examples of training topics include phishing awareness, incident response, regulatory compliance, data privacy, social media platform awareness, etc. Appropriate delivery methods should also be adopted having regard to the B/D’s size, risks, resources, and the target audience’s needs. The training approach may include presentations, videos, interactive modules, practical exercises, and case studies.", "bbox": [ 184, 580, 880, 696 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(iv) Evaluation of the effectiveness of training activities", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 715, 653, 732 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should review the effectiveness of the training activities. An assessment may be conducted to ensure user awareness of information security requirements and responsibilities. This can be done through methods such as post-training quizzes, feedback surveys, simulation exercises, and observing changes in behaviour or the number of security incidents to evaluate knowledge gain, behavioural changes, and participant satisfaction.", "bbox": [ 184, 736, 868, 837 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(v) Regular review and update", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 186, 854, 453, 871 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds should continuously review and update the training programme to reflect the evolving threat landscape, new technologies, and changes in regulations and", "bbox": [ 186, 873, 860, 909 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 117, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "header", "text": "HUMAN RESOURCE SECURITY", "bbox": [ 621, 49, 880, 64 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "31", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 41 }, { "type": "text", "text": "compliance requirements. In addition, B/Ds should make reference to the feedback to identify improvement areas and adjust or fine-tune the training programme.", "bbox": [ 184, 91, 870, 126 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(d) Personnel Security", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 145, 373, 165 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Classified information shall be protected from unauthorised access or unauthorised disclosure. Officers shall not publish, make private copies of or communicate to unauthorised persons any classified document or information obtained in their official capacity unless they are required to do so in the interest of the Government. The “need to know” principle shall be applied to all classified information, which shall be provided only to persons who require it for the efficient discharge of their work and who have authorised access. If in any doubt as to whether an officer has authorised access to a particular document, classification or information, the Departmental Security Officer should be consulted.", "bbox": [ 184, 186, 867, 337 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall ensure that personnel security risks are effectively managed. B/Ds shall assess the risk of allowing an individual to access classified information.", "bbox": [ 186, 357, 867, 392 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Access to classified information higher than RESTRICTED is restricted to civil servants who have undergone appropriate integrity checks. B/Ds should consult the departmental personnel section about the Integrity Checking Instructions. For staff other than civil servants, appropriate background verification checks should be carried out commensurate with the business requirements, the classification of the information that the staff will handle, and the perceived risks. Background verification checks may include the following having addressed any personal privacy issues:", "bbox": [ 184, 413, 872, 548 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Independent identity check (Hong Kong Identity Card or passport).", "bbox": [ 188, 570, 771, 588 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Confirmation of claimed academic and professional qualifications.", "bbox": [ 188, 592, 771, 609 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Completeness and accuracy check of the provided curriculum vitae.", "bbox": [ 188, 613, 776, 631 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": " Availability of employment references.", "bbox": [ 188, 636, 547, 652 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "More detailed checks, such as credit checks or checks of criminal records, if considered necessary.", "bbox": [ 188, 656, 848, 690 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(e) Clear Policies and Procedures", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 720, 477, 739 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Management shall establish clear policies and supporting procedures regarding the use of information systems so as to set out clearly the allowed and disallowed actions on their information systems. These actions should normally be covered in the departmental IT Security Policy. The departmental IT Security Policy shall include a provision advising staff that if they contravene any provision of the policy, they may be subject to different levels of disciplinary or punitive actions depending on the severity of the breach. Staff shall be formally notified of their authorisation to access an information system as well as their responsibilities and duties on these information systems.", "bbox": [ 184, 756, 877, 904 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "32", "bbox": [ 860, 927, 880, 940 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 49, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "header", "text": "HUMAN RESOURCE SECURITY", "bbox": [ 621, 49, 880, 64 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 115, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 42 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(f) IT Security Responsibilities after Termination or Change of Employment", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 114, 90, 759, 130 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Post-employment responsibilities and duties shall be defined in the terms and conditions of employment. The communication of termination responsibilities to the staff shall include continuing information security requirements and legal responsibilities. The communication of termination responsibilities should also include responsibilities stipulated in any confidentiality agreement and the terms and conditions of employment continuing for a defined period after the end of employment. Changes of responsibility or employment shall be managed as the termination of the current responsibility or employment followed by the commencement of the new responsibility or employment.", "bbox": [ 184, 146, 882, 296 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "header", "text": "IT SECURITY GUIDELINES", "bbox": [ 115, 48, 341, 64 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "header", "text": "HUMAN RESOURCE SECURITY", "bbox": [ 621, 49, 880, 64 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "footer", "text": "Ref. No.: G3", "bbox": [ 117, 927, 213, 941 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "page_number", "text": "33", "bbox": [ 858, 927, 880, 941 ], "page_idx": 43 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10. ASSET MANAGEMENT", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 105, 453, 124 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "B/Ds shall maintain appropriate protection of all the hardware, software and information assets and ensure that information receives an appropriate level of protection.", "bbox": [ 186, 147, 831, 198 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "10.1 Responsibility for Assets", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 117, 221, 431, 241 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "(a) Inventory of Assets", "text_level": 2, "bbox": [ 115, 267, 379, 287 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Inventory of assets helps ensure that effective protection takes place and identifies lost assets. Regardless of the source of funding of information systems, an inventory shall be drawn up of all information systems including infrastructure facilities and departmental shared IT services (with their system classifications), hardware assets, software assets, valid warranties, service agreements and legal/contractual documents (e.g. public domain name registrations and related IP addresses, physical locations of data storage, etc.). Periodic review of the inventory shall be conducted to ensure that the assets are properly owned, kept and maintained. To better manage the software supply chain, B/Ds should gather as much information as possible about the associated components of the software assets (e.g. supplier, component name, version, dependency relation, etc.).", "bbox": [ 184, 306, 880, 489 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "In particular, DITSO shall maintain an up-to-date inventory of all Internet-facing services of their B/Ds. The inventory shall be comprehensive and include at least the description, IP addresses, domain names, and network ports opened of the services which are exposed to the Internet.", "bbox": [ 184, 510, 853, 577 ], "page_idx": 44 }, { "type": "text", "text": "Asset ownership shall be assigned when assets are created or transferred from other parties.
